Cyclical time points

Source: R/cyclical_time.R
cyclical_time.Rd

cyclical_time() creates a vector of cyclical time points representing positions within repeating cycles. This function is useful for creating custom cyclical time representations that aren't covered by the convenience functions like day_of_week() or month_of_year().

Usage

cyclical_time(
  data,
  chronon = time_chronon(data),
  cycle = time_cycle(data),
  discrete = TRUE,
  calendar = time_calendar(data)
)

Arguments

data

Input data to convert to cyclical time. Can be:

  • Numeric values: underspecified cyclical time (positions with no enclosing cycle), counted the way the chronon is displayed (e.g. 3 is March for months of the year, 0 is midnight for seconds of the day). Positions beyond the longest possible cycle (e.g. day 32 of a month) are NA.

  • Character strings (parsed as dates/times)

  • Date or POSIXct objects

  • Other time objects

chronon

A time granule representing the chronon (finest indivisible time granule), evaluated in the context of calendar. Use unquoted expressions like day(1L) or month(1L). Chronons from a specific calendar can also be used (e.g. cal_isoweek$day(1L)).

cycle

A time granule representing the cycle (coarser time granule that defines the period), evaluated in the context of calendar. Use unquoted expressions like week(1L) or year(1L).

discrete

Logical. If TRUE (default), returns integer positions within the cycle (discrete time model). If FALSE, returns fractional positions allowing representation of fractional time chronons (continuous time model).

calendar

Calendar system used to evaluate chronon and cycle. Defaults to time_calendar(data) for existing time objects. Common options include cal_gregorian and cal_isoweek.

Value

A mixtime time vector of located cyclical time (mt_cyclical), or underspecified cyclical time (mt_cyclical_free) for numeric data.

Located and underspecified cyclical time

A cyclical time point is a position within a cycle, such as March within a year. The cycle it falls in (which year) is its enclosing cycle, and whether that is known gives two types of cyclical time:

  • Located cyclical time knows its enclosing cycle. It is created from time points: month_of_year(as.Date("2024-03-15")) is March 2024, displayed as Mar.

  • Underspecified cyclical time doesn't. It is created from positions: month_of_year(3) is March of any year.

Both compare and sort by their position within the cycle, so month_of_year(3) == month_of_year(as.Date("2024-03-15")) is TRUE.

They differ in operations that move a position. Located cyclical time moves its underlying time point, so the result accounts for the enclosing cycle: adding a day to day_of_month(as.Date(c("2023-02-28", "2024-02-28"))) gives D01 D29.

Underspecified cyclical time only supports operations that don't need its enclosing cycle, and which those are depends on the cycle's length:

  • Fixed-length cycles (e.g. months of the year, days of the week) wrap around: month_of_year(12) + 1 is Jan.

  • Variable-length cycles (e.g. days of the month or year) can't be moved: day_of_month(28) + 1 is day 29, or day 1 of a non-leap February, so it is an error. Positions are only checked against the longest cycle, so day_of_month(31) is valid but day_of_month(32) is NA.

Locate underspecified cyclical time in a specific enclosing cycle with time_compose(): adding a day to time_compose(yearmonth("2024-02"), day_of_month(28)) gives 2024-02-29. The two types can't be cast into each other. See mt_cyclical_free-arithmetic and mt_cyclical_free-compare for details.

See also

  • new_cyclical_time_fn() for creating reusable cyclical time functions

  • day_of_week(), day_of_month(), day_of_year() for common cyclical representations

  • month_of_year(), week_of_year() for other cyclical time helpers

  • cal_gregorian, cal_isoweek for calendar systems

Examples

# Day of week (1-7, Monday = 1)
cyclical_time(
  Sys.Date(),
  chronon = day(1L),
  cycle = week(1L),
  calendar = cal_isoweek
)
#> <mixtime[1]>
#> [1] Thu

# Month of year (1-12)
cyclical_time(
  Sys.Date(),
  chronon = month(1L),
  cycle = year(1L)
)
#> <mixtime[1]>
#> [1] Nov

# Continuous time (discrete = FALSE) for fractional month of year
cyclical_time(
  Sys.Date(),
  chronon = month(1L),
  cycle = year(1L),
  discrete = FALSE
)
#> <mixtime[1]>
#> [1] Nov 83.3%

# Day of month with Gregorian calendar
cyclical_time(
  Sys.Date(),
  chronon = day(1L),
  cycle = month(1L),
  calendar = cal_gregorian
)
#> <mixtime[1]>
#> [1] D26

# Hours, minutes, and seconds
cyclical_time(
  Sys.time(),
  chronon = second(1L),
  cycle = day(1L)
)
#> <mixtime[1]>
#> [1] 02:56:39
#' # Underspecified cyclical time from positions
month_of_year(c(3, 12)) + 1
#> <mixtime[2]>
#> [1] Apr Jan
try(day_of_month(28) + 1)
#> Error : Can't add 1 day to a day of month in an unknown month.
#> ✖ The number of days in a month varies, so where a day of month lands after
#>   adding 1 day depends on which month it is in.
#> ℹ Locate it in a specific month first, e.g. `time_compose(yearmonth("2024-02"),
#>   x) + days(1)`.
time_compose(yearmonth("2024-02"), day_of_month(28)) + days(1)
#> <mixtime[1]>
#> [1] 2024-02-29

# Located cyclical time moves with its enclosing cycle
day_of_month(as.Date(c("2023-02-28", "2024-02-28"))) + days(1)
#> <mixtime[2]>
#> [1] D01 D29
